segments.english: Question: one of the students asked, and these are his words: "Let our teacher inform us: the worship and the prayer that we pray, to whom it pertains. To the Cause of causes, blessed be He, or to the emanated being that was emanated from Him (Ze'ir Anpin), as explained to us in your hearing by our teacher Salem son of David, who travelled from here to the Holy Land, according to the true faith, as explained in the book Matzref ha-Emunah and in a book on the Torah, that whoever worships Ein Sof worships without a God of truth and without a God of judgment, so that we may know whom we shall worship. And your reply, speedily, my lord. Thus far."

grammar: שאול שאל is an infinitive absolute before a finite verb: 'asking, he asked'. The heading of the correspondence is 'Question' (decisions).
וז״ל introduces the quotation, which runs to ע״כ at the end; the question is one long quoted sentence-chain.
The question offers two objects of worship joined by או, 'or': the Cause of causes, or the emanated being. The או sets them as alternatives.
שהעובד לאין סוף עובד ללא אלהי אמת: the participle שהעובד is the subject, 'whoever worships Ein Sof', and the verb repeats as 'worships'.
כדי שנדע את מי נעבוד: את is the object marker before מי, 'whom'; the purpose clause closes the question.
segments.note: The quotation runs from וז״ל to ע״כ. The parentheses around ז״א are the writer's and stay in parentheses inside the quotation.
apparatus: 2 Chr 15:3: 'לְלֹא אֱלֹהֵי אֱמֶת', 'without the true God', is echoed in ללא אלהי אמת (2:2.49-51); the English keeps 'without a God of truth'.
Isa 30:18: 'כִּי אֱלֹהֵי מִשְׁפָּט ה׳', 'for the LORD is a God of judgment', is echoed in אלהי משפט (2:2.53-54).
עה״ת (2:2.44) is read as על התורה, 'on the Torah'. It occurs only here, and the work it names is not identified.

grammar: The reply is the respondent's letter, quoted in double marks from 'Your reply' to the closing 'Thus far'; the verse inside it is in single marks.
ישמע חכם ויוסף לקח is Prov 1:5, quoted without a formula. The yiqtol ישמע is read as the verse's future, 'will hear'.
והמקובל בידינו שהעבודה לאל אדון אחד: the participle phrase is the subject of 'is that worship is to one Lord'; the English puts it first.
להמשיך השפע ממנו אל עשר ספירות: the infinitive gives the purpose of the worship, to draw the flow from Him to the ten sefirot.
כמו שכתב לחם שלמה: 'as Lechem Shlomo wrote'; a book cited by its title, with no reference given.
segments.note: The respondent's answer to the question in 2:2; its closing formula עכ״ל closes the quotation.

segments.english: The questioner replied again. Your reply, my friend, came closed and sealed, and in it there is nothing but an indication of a place: "to study in Kisse Eliyahu, from folio 13 to folio 18, 'A wise man will hear and add to learning,' and what we have received is that worship is to God, one Lord, etc." I did not understand your opinion and your intention in this, whether this, what you have received, is in accordance with the words of Kisse Eliyahu or the opposite of his words. For when I studied in Kisse Eliyahu the place you marked for me, I did not find what I sought; on the contrary, there, on folio 3, he compares the oneness of the Creator to the other kinds of oneness, where he wrote: "Just as this house as a whole is called by the name one house. And if you enter it, you will find many rooms, large and small, and many other places. And each and every one of them ascribes to it a designation, one name. Also, a wooden building that has several attributes within it has them. Also, you will find further that this holy wall, which was built, was in parts; each and every stone was separate from the clods of earth, by itself, and the lime by itself, etc. And after the builder came and joined all these parts with his wisdom, this within that, and this beside that, and they became one wall, etc., thus, then, all is one piece and one part. And so is the matter with us, etc." And there, on folios 25 and 29, he compares it to the human body, joined of bones and sinews and flesh, head and eye and ear and nose and mouth and hands and feet, and the whole is called by the name man, Reuben or Simeon. And on folios 25, 26 and 27 he wrote: "The sum of the matter is that the First Cause, which is called Ein Sof by all the Kabbalists, is He who emanated, created, formed and made, and He is hidden within Ze'ir Anpin, and then Ze'ir Anpin is the one who rules over all creatures, leads them, feeds them and sustains them, by the power of Ein Sof within him. Therefore He is our God, and we are His people, for our souls are His portion, and Him we shall worship, and He is the God of our fathers, in whose hand is the conduct of the worlds, for reward and punishment. But Ein Sof, with the other partzufim above Ze'ir and his Nukva, if human beings order their prayers to them individually, without praying to Ze'ir Anpin, even if they direct their intention to the soul hidden in them, they will cry out and not be answered. And on the contrary, those who pray to them will be punished, for it is the will of the First Cause that He be the one who brings out and brings in His flow to the lower beings, and there is no other besides Him. See there carefully." And the words of the Rabbi, the author of Kisse Eliyahu, stand against the words of the Rambam, of blessed memory, in his commentary on the Mishnah, in his composition, and in Moreh Nevukhim, and against the words of the pious one, the author of Chovot ha-Levavot, in the Gate of Unity, and Rabbi Saadia Gaon in the book Emunot ve-De'ot, and the Roke'ach, who wrote that His oneness, may He be blessed, is not like the one of a pair, nor like the one of a species, nor like the one man who is divided into many ones. And not one like a simple body, etc., which receives division without end. But the Name, may He be blessed, is one with a oneness that has no like. Also, Kisse Eliyahu wrote that Ein Sof is the soul of Atik, and Arikh Anpin, and Abba and Imma, and Ze'ir and his Nukva, and my teachers, of blessed memory, the aforesaid, wrote that He is not a body, nor a force in a body! And according to his words He is a force in a body. Also he wrote that Arikh Anpin, Abba and Imma preceded Ze'ir Anpin who is our God (according to his words), and he is called a son of Abba and Imma, etc. And our Rabbis of blessed memory said that He is eternal before all that exists, and that every existent other than Him is not eternal, etc. Also he wrote concerning Ein Sof, blessed be He, that no worship pertains to Him, and no invocation at all. And no name applies to Him: not YHVH, nor Adonai, etc. but only to Ze'ir Anpin and his Nukva in the World of Emanation alone, and not to Arikh Anpin, Abba and Imma, and Ze'ir and his Nukva that are in the emanated worlds above the World of Emanation, as explained there, 4, 49, the end of side a, and on folio 53....

tokens.note: וכו׳ = etc.: the quotation is cut short and 'etc.' is kept (decisions)

tokens.gloss: in accordance with the words of

tokens.note: שם read as 'there', the place in the book; see apparatus
ג׳ is folio 3
אחדות (oneness) is kept distinct from יחוד (unity)
א׳ is written with an apostrophe; in כל א׳ ואחד it is 'one', rendered 'each and every one'
האציל, the verb of אצילות (emanation), kept distinct from ברא (create)
זעיר: 'small', from Ze'ir Anpin, literally 'small face'
ונוקביה: his Nukva, literally 'female'
ע״ש: עיין שם, 'see there' (not על שם, 'on account of').
הר׳ = הרב, 'the Rabbi'; the title stands before the book's name and means its author, as the Rabbi Etz Yosef at 2:9 and at 4:19 (cf. 'Kisse Eliyahu wrote' below).
הרמב״ם: the Rambam, of blessed memory
ובחבור: 'and in his composition'; החבור is the usual name of the Rambam's Mishneh Torah (the text does not name it).
מורה נבוכים: Moreh Nevukhim, literally 'Guide of the Perplexed'
חובת הלבבות: Chovot ha-Levavot, literally 'Duties of the Hearts'
אמונות ודעות: Emunot ve-De'ot, literally 'Beliefs and Opinions'
ית׳ = יתברך, 'may He be blessed'

tokens.gloss: the Name, may He be blessed
tokens.note: השי״ת: 'the Name, may He be blessed'
עתיק: Atik, literally 'ancient'; a partzuf.
ארוך: Arikh, 'long'; Arikh Anpin, 'long face'
אבא: Abba, literally 'father'; a partzuf.
אימא: Imma, literally 'mother'; a partzuf.

tokens.gloss: and our Rabbis of blessed memory

tokens.note: קדמון: 'eternal'; the decisions give the note 'without beginning'
ב״ה: 'blessed be He'
הוי״ה: the Name YHVH, as a name
אדנות: literally 'lordship'
לז״א: to Ze'ir Anpin
לא״א: to Arikh Anpin (א״א)
ד׳: 4, the folio

grammar: The paragraph is the questioner's reply. The respondent's words and Kisse Eliyahu are quoted in double marks; a verse inside them is in single marks.
ולא הבנתי דעתך וכוונתך בזה, אם זה ... או היפך דבריו: an indirect question, 'whether ... or ...', with אם introducing the first alternative.
אדרבא שם: 'on the contrary' reverses what was expected; the book says the opposite of what the questioner sought.
Indirect reports introduced by כתב ש- or כתבו ש- (for example 'Also he wrote that ...') carry no quotation marks; only the direct formula כתב: opens a quotation.
ואין עוד מלבדו is an embedded verse (Deut 4:35, 4:39), translated from its Hebrew as 'there is no other besides Him'.
segments.note: The questioner's second letter (חזר השואל והשיב). The Wikisource text ends mid-sentence ('....') and the English keeps the break.
apparatus: Prov 1:5 (2:4.22–25): 'ישמע חכם ויוסף לקח', rendered as the verse's future.
שם (2:4.61) is read as 'there', the place in the book; the other sense, 'the name', does not fit the sentence.
The author writes ארוך (2:4.365) and שאריך (2:4.387) for Arikh; both are rendered Arikh Anpin.
ד׳ (2:4.460) is read as 4, the folio; the numeral is kept because the author writes דף in full nearby.
Deut 6:13: 'ואתו תעבד', 'and Him you shall worship', is echoed in ואותו נעבוד (2:4.236-237), with the verb in the first person plural.
